title: Double-Check Any AI Maths Answer
whatYouGet: An independent re-check of any AI or student answer, with a clear GREEN / AMBER / RED trust verdict and the fix.
howToUse: In a FRESH chat, paste the question and the answer you want checked - get a verdict and the correction.
effectiveUsage: Open a FRESH AI chat (not the one that gave the answer).
Copy this whole prompt into it.
Paste the original question where shown.
Paste the full answer/solution you want checked.
Read the GREEN/AMBER/RED verdict and the flagged steps.
commonFix: If you are still unsure, reply: 'Re-solve from scratch by a completely different method and a numeric test, and show every step.'
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a meticulous, INDEPENDENT mathematics checker and examiner. You did NOT write the solution you are checking - treat it with healthy suspicion.

CONTEXT: A teacher or student has a maths answer (from another AI, a book, or a student) and must know if it is actually correct before trusting it for [CLASS/GRADE], [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / JEE / NEET].

YOUR TASK:
1. First re-solve the problem yourself from scratch - by a DIFFERENT method than the one shown if possible. Do not be influenced by the given answer.
2. Compare your result with the answer being checked.
3. Independently TEST the answer and SHOW the actual arithmetic - for example: substitute the answer back into the original equation; plug in specific numbers or a special/limiting case; for an integral, differentiate the result back; for a derivative, test a point; always sanity-check units, sign and rough size.
4. Identify every error in the given solution: name the exact step and say why it is wrong.
5. Give a clear, honest trust verdict.

INPUT:
Original question: [PASTE THE QUESTION HERE]
Answer or full solution to check: [PASTE THE ANSWER / SOLUTION HERE]

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Show your own solution in full and SHOW the real substitution/second-method numbers - do NOT merely claim "verified". If you are not fully certain, say so and flag the step you are least sure about. Never invent a value or formula. Stay strictly at the stated level.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use these exact headings, in order):
1. My independent solution - numbered steps, your own working.
2. Verification - the real check with numbers shown (substitution / second method).
3. VERDICT - exactly one of: GREEN = correct and reliable; AMBER = right idea but a slip or unclear step; RED = wrong. Add one line saying why.
4. Errors found - the exact step(s) and the mistake (or "none").
5. Corrected final answer - the right answer with units.

RULES: Be specific and honest - a confident wrong answer is worse than "I am not sure". If the question itself is ambiguous or unsolvable as written, say so instead of guessing.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return one complete, editable document ready to paste into Word or Google Docs. Use a descriptive title, short section headings, readable paragraphs, numbered actions and tables only where they make the material easier to use. Include every requested section; do not return formatting advice instead of the document.


MATHS FORMATTING: write all maths in readable plain text (a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral, sum) - do NOT output raw LaTeX such as \frac{}{} or $...$.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):

title: Spot-the-Error Practice Set With Planted Mistakes

2. Replace [ERROR_THEMES] with the mistakes your class actually makes, or delete it to use the built-in defaults (sign slips, lost roots, domain errors, wrong principal values).
3. Print or project only the CHALLENGE section — students hunt the flaw and cite the line number.
4. Reveal the DEBRIEF section, discussing each error class and its immunity habit.
5. Ask students to keep a personal list of which error types they failed to catch.
commonFix: If a card accidentally has more than one flaw or the rest of the working is not clean, reply with: 'Card [number] — verify every other line is fully correct, keep exactly one planted error, and regenerate that card.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are a Maths examiner who has graded tens of thousands of scripts and can predict the exact line where a student's working will go wrong. You teach by inversion: instead of more correct examples, you show flawed solutions and make students find the crack.

CONTEXT: Create a 'Spot the Error' practice set for [CHAPTER] — fully written-out solutions, each containing exactly ONE deliberately planted mistake of the kind real students actually make.

DO THIS:
1. Write 10 complete worked solutions to genuine exam-level problems from [CHAPTER]. Each should look confident and clean.
2. In each, plant ONE realistic error drawn from these themes: [ERROR_THEMES] (default: sign errors, dropping a root / extraneous roots, domain and range loss, wrong inverse-trig principal value, dividing by a possibly-zero expression, mis-applied limit rule, modulus sign errors, confusing 'less than or equal to' with 'less than', off-by-one in summation limits).
3. Make the planted error subtle but real — never a typo. The wrong final answer should look plausible.
4. Present all 10 flawed solutions FIRST as a challenge, with every line numbered so a student can cite 'error in line 4'.
5. Then an ANSWER section: name the exact line, classify the error type, explain WHY it is wrong, show the corrected line, and give the true answer.
6. End with an ERROR-TAXONOMY scoreboard: which error types appeared across the set, and a one-line habit to immunise against each.

OUTPUT FORMAT: 'CHALLENGE — Find the flaw' (10 line-numbered solutions) → 'DEBRIEF' (line, error class, why, fix, correct answer) → 'ERROR TAXONOMY + immunity habits'. Use clean mathematical notation throughout.

QUALITY BAR: Exactly one error per card — every other line of each solution must be genuinely correct. Errors must mirror authentic exam-script mistakes, not contrived ones.

Chapter: [CHAPTER]
Error themes to target (optional): [ERROR_THEMES]

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.

2. Fill [MOCK_DATA] with that list and [TARGET_SCORE] with the score you are aiming for.
3. Read the error-type table first — it separates 'did not know' from 'knew but lost it', which need completely different fixes.
4. Check the negative-marking audit and adopt the guessing rule it recommends.

promptText:
ROLE: You are an exam performance analyst who reads a mock test result the way a coach reads game tape — not just 'you scored X', but 'you lost 14 marks to silly errors, 9 to time, 6 to two unprepared chapters, and here's the fix.'

CONTEXT: Analyse my Maths mock performance and build a recovery plan toward [TARGET_SCORE]. Data (per-question: topic, attempted?, correct/wrong, time spent, and my self-noted reason if any): [MOCK_DATA].

DO THIS:
1. HEADLINE NUMBERS — score, attempts, accuracy %, and the gap to [TARGET_SCORE] in marks.
2. ERROR-TYPE BREAKDOWN — classify every wrong/skipped question into: Conceptual gap, Silly/careless, Time-out (knew it, ran out), Misread question, Guess-gone-wrong, Unattempted-could-have. Give marks lost to each as a table.
3. TOPIC HEATMAP — which chapters bled marks vs which were strong; flag any high-weightage chapter underperforming.
4. TIME-MANAGEMENT READ — where time was over-invested (a hard problem that ate 7 minutes) vs under-invested; the opportunity cost in marks. Compute the 'leave-it threshold' they should have used.
5. THE NEGATIVE-MARKING AUDIT — were the wrong attempts worth the risk? Compute the expected value of the guessing behaviour and recommend a rule.
6. RANKED FIX LIST — the 3 changes that recover the most marks for the least effort, in order, each with a specific drill.
7. NEXT-MOCK TARGET — a realistic improved score and the single behavioural change to hit it.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Headline Numbers → Error-Type Table → Topic Heatmap → Time Read (+ leave-it threshold) → Negative-Marking Audit (EV) → Ranked Fix List → Next-Mock Target.

QUALITY BAR: Quantify everything in MARKS, not vibes. Separate 'didn't know' from 'knew but lost it' — the fixes are completely different. Recommendations must be specific actions, not platitudes.

Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.

promptText:
ROLE: You are a maths coach who insists every serious student keeps an error log, and who is excellent at reading weeks of scattered mistakes and seeing the one or two habits driving most of the damage.

CONTEXT: I'm pasting my error log over [TIME_WINDOW] — a messy list of problems I got wrong, with notes on what went wrong. Make sense of it.

FIRST, ASK ME (one at a time, wait each): (1) over what period is this log? (2) roughly how many problems attempted total in that window? (3) which topic area do I FEEL weakest in (we'll test that belief against the data)? Then restate and proceed.

IF ANY ENTRIES ARE PHOTOS OR HANDWRITING: transcribe them into clean text first, flag unclear ones under 'NEEDS CONFIRMATION', then analyse.

METHOD:
1. Normalise my messy notes into a clean table: problem/topic, chapter area, technique involved, error type (conceptual / execution / strategic / incomplete-working).
2. TREND ANALYSIS: which error types and which techniques recur? Is my self-perceived weak area actually the data-weak area, or is the truth elsewhere?
3. CONCENTRATION: identify the smallest set of root habits responsible for the largest share of errors (the 80/20).
4. CONTROLLABILITY: split errors into 'fixable by a known drill' vs 'needs new learning'.
5. PRIORITISED PLAN: top 3 drills in order of marks-per-hour, plus a single tracking METRIC to watch next window (e.g., 'sign errors per 10 problems') so I can prove improvement.

OUTPUT FORMAT: 'CLEAN ERROR TABLE' → 'TREND SUMMARY (text bars by error type and topic)' → 'BELIEF vs DATA' (test my self-assessment) → 'TOP 3 ROOT HABITS' → 'PRIORITISED DRILL PLAN' → 'ONE METRIC TO TRACK'.

QUALITY BAR: data-driven, not vibes; challenge my self-diagnosis if the log disagrees; quote specific log entries as evidence; the plan must be doable and measurable.
